cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: Both studies involving High-Entropy Alloys (FeNiCrMn and CoNiCrFeMn) identify a coexistence of Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod dislocations under tensile deformation, with stair-rod dislocations often associated with Lomer-Cottrell locks or immobile behavior.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: One study (PMC12029629) focuses on identifying these dislocations using the Dislocation Extraction Algorithm (DXA) and Coordination Number Analysis (CNA) in MD simulations of FeNiCrMn but explicitly notes a lack of detail regarding the specific DXA parameter thresholds or CNA differentiation criteria in the text. The other study (PMC8398136) attributes the immobility of the a/6[011] stair-rod to geometric incompatibility, noting its Burgers vector lies outside the active slip planes.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The immobility of the a/6[011] stair-rod is described as dependent on the specific slip planes active in the observed deformation mode (Figure 6 context). The formation of Lomer-Cottrell locks is observed in FeNiCrMn under tensile loading.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no direct contradictions between the papers; however, the first paper explicitly states it does not provide the specific atomic configuration or DXA criteria that the other paper implies are known or observable in Figure 6. The first paper infers the existence of Lomer-Cottrell locks without detailing the configuration, while the second paper attributes immobility to geometric constraints.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: The evidence for the classification of dislocations is observational (DXA/CNA results) but methodological details are weak in the FeNiCrMn study. The explanation for immobility in the CoNiCrFeMn study is based on specific simulation conditions.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The specific atomic configuration of the stair-rod dislocations that leads to Lomer-Cottrell locks is not described in the FeNiCrMn study. Furthermore, the specific DXA distinguishing criteria (parameter thresholds) and CNA visual differentiation methods for these dislocations remain unspecified in the available text.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The immobility of stair-rod dislocations in HEAs is primarily a geometric constraint where the resultant Burgers vector does not lie on the active slip planes, preventing glide, though the precise atomic signature used to distinguish them computationally remains undocumented in the FeNiCrMn analysis.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: A comparative MD study should explicitly report the vector algebra criteria used in DXA to filter a/6<110> (stair-rod) from a/6<112> (Shockley) dislocations and correlate these with the local atomic coordination to verify if CNA can visually differentiate them based on coordination number changes specific to the stair-rod core structure.
